scope: Read-only runs against the owner's real stores on the owner's host while the owner's claude-mem worker and three chroma-mcp processes ran. Diagnostic observations, not gate evidence. Every run was traced with strace (-f, seccomp, -s 0, no payload bytes) for opens, writes, renames, unlinks, mode and time changes, links and signals; proof/VELDO-0182/README.md, Round 2, explains each.

environment.uv_constraint: UV_CONSTRAINT named a file holding 'pydantic<2.14'. A fresh uvx resolution of chroma-mcp on 2026-10-09 picks pydantic 2.14.0, with which chroma-mcp's mcp 1.6.0 fails to import (eval_type_backport). The owner's running chroma-mcp still uses pydantic 2.13.5, resolved on 2026-10-05; a restart of the owner's claude-mem would meet the same failure. The check passes UV_ settings and the owner's uv.toml through to the dedicated chroma-mcp, and without a working chroma-mcp it refuses unavailable_service:memory:claude_mem:adapter.

safety_copies.note: copy_data for all five parts into a private scratch directory; each SQLite database's integrity_check and counts in the copy against the source before and after; each Chroma copy loaded by chromadb 1.5.5 from the owner's mem0 venv.

claude_mem_check.after_note: Final implementation. Most of the after run is the dedicated worker's own Chroma backfill, which a search awaits when a sampled memory is not found at first. An earlier diagnostic run over 20 other random memories showed this directly: one user prompt absent from the owner's Chroma was found after that backfill (435 s), and the other 19 in 0.5 to 8 s each.
claude_mem_check.sample_mix: 20 of 79469: 9 observations, 6 session summaries, 5 user prompts; 0 without indexed text

loss_on_a_copy.how: A private copy of the real store with the first sampled memory renumbered (count unchanged), checked with after; the real worker and search server refused it.

owner_processes: The owner's claude-mem worker (pid 10845, started 2026-09-01), its two mcp-server.cjs and three chroma-mcp process pairs were listed before and after every run and were unchanged; no process carrying a check's private HOME remained.
incident: During the first copy verification, a read-only count opened ~/projects/myday/knowledge_graph/knowledge_graph.db (WAL mode, held open by no one) with mode=ro&readonly_shm=1, and SQLite created an empty knowledge_graph.db-wal beside it (0 bytes, 2026-10-09 08:48:18 local). Nothing else was written. The file was left in place for the owner. The copy now reads such an idle database immutably (copy/idle-wal-no-sidecars), and every later traced run opened nothing under the stores for writing except SQLite's read-only connection opening the existing claude-mem.db-wal, through which nothing was written.
